description: Notification and app badge outcomes (B09, WebCore #117). Chromium values come from tests/abi/notifications_browser.mjs; native values from tests/abi/notifications.py. A qualified case records where the engines differ and why; a native value of null is browser-only evidence.

default-permission.qualification: Automated Chromium reports denied before any grant; a native host starts at default and the application sets the permission.

fields.qualification: A native document's base URL is about:blank, so the native probe passes an absolute icon URL; a relative one resolves to no icon, which the probe also checks.

defaults.qualification: An unset silent reads false in Chromium and null in WebKit, as the nullable IDL attribute specifies.

missing-title.qualification: The native title is a required argument; the managed contract rejects a null title.

actions.qualification: Actions belong to persistent notifications, which no target provides; the managed contract has no actions.

bad-dir.qualification: Native rejects a dir outside RV_NOTIFICATION_DIR_* with RV_ERR_UNSUPPORTED.

badge-set.qualification: Badges are managed only: the application's handler receives them.

badge-negative.qualification: As badge-set; the managed count is an unsigned 64-bit value.

request-granted.qualification: Native permission is the application's setting, not a prompt.

show-granted.qualification: Headless Chromium has no notification presenter, so a granted show fires error. A native presenter shows it; the probe reports show, click and, after the cancel request, close.
